behaviour: Adds unit tests that arrowhead geometry follows arrowheadSize and that the short-segment fitting still caps it.
rules: 1. Add getArrowheadSizeScale to the existing import from "../src/bounds".

Append a describe("arrowhead size") block at the end of the file; its helper creates an arrow with API.createElement({ type: "arrow", points, endArrowhead: "arrow", roughness: 0, arrowheadSize }) and returns getArrowheadPoints(arrow, ShapeCache.generateElementShape(arrow, null), "end", "arrow")!.
3. A head's width is pointDistance of its side ends (indices 2-3 and 4-5 of the returned array); its length is the distance from the tip (indices 0-1) to the midpoint of the side ends.

behaviour: jsdom tests for the arrowhead size: restore and SVG export, the export frame for large heads, the panel control and undo on the full, compact and mobile layouts, canvas padding, and copy/paste styles.
rules: 1. Imports: pointFrom and type LocalPoint from "@excalidraw/math"; getArrowheadPoints, getCanvasPadding and ShapeCache from "@excalidraw/element"; types from "@excalidraw/element/types"; actionCopyStyles and actionPasteStyles from "../actions/actionStyles"; serializeAsJSON from "../data/json"; restoreElements from "../data/restore"; Excalidraw from "../index"; exportScene from "../scene/export"; API from "./helpers/api"; Keyboard from "./helpers/ui"; act, fireEvent, render, screen, waitFor from "./test-utils".

2. `const { h } = window;`; describe("arrowhead size") renders <Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} /> in beforeEach and flushes with `await act(async () => {})` in afterEach, as freedrawMode.test.tsx does; a second top-level describe("arrowhead size in compact and mobile panels") has no beforeEach and renders per case, as drawShape.test.tsx's compact toolbar test does.

3. A file-level helper makeArrow(overrides) returns API.createElement({ type: "arrow", x: 0, y: 0, width: 200, height: 0, points: [pointFrom<LocalPoint>(0, 0), pointFrom<LocalPoint>(200, 0)], endArrowhead: "arrow", roughness: 0, ...overrides }).

4. A file-level helper getSvgHeadSpread(svg) collects the numbers of every path's d attribute in the exported SVG, takes the odd-indexed ones (y coordinates), and returns max minus min; the shaft is flat, so the spread is the head's width.

5. The scene is set with API.setElements and the selection with API.setSelectedElements; actions run through API.executeAction; undo is Keyboard.undo(); the latest element is read back from h.elements by id.
6. The panel is driven through screen.queryByTestId / getByTestId with the testIds "arrowheadSize-small", "arrowheadSize-medium", "arrowheadSize-large" and fireEvent.click.

7. Head equality in the paste case compares getArrowheadPoints(element, ShapeCache.generateElementShape(element, null), "end", "arrow") of target and source with toEqual; both are created with the same points, so only their size can differ.
8. The SVG frame height is Number(svg.getAttribute("height")); exports use no config, so the padding is the default 10px on each side.

9. The compact/mobile case uses it.each(["tablet", "phone"] as const): render <Excalidraw UIOptions={{ getFormFactor: () => formFactor }} />, fireEvent.resize(window), await waitFor until h.app.editorInterface.formFactor is formFactor, set and select the arrow, open the popover with API.setAppState({ openPopup: "compactArrowProperties" }), then await waitFor on the testId query; waitFor comes from "./test-utils" with the other test utilities.
